economy.summary: His campaign says families across the region are being squeezed by rising costs, taxes, and failing governmental policies, and that his focus is affordability, responsible government, and accountability in Harrisburg so working families can keep more of what they earn.
economy.short: Says families squeezed by rising costs; focuses on affordability.

taxes.summary: In his February 2026 campaign announcement he called for policies that allow families to build stable lives without being taxed out of their livelihoods.
taxes.short: Calls for policies so families aren't taxed out of livelihoods.

economy.summary: His campaign platform calls for investing in and supporting small businesses and Main Streets, and advocating for wages that sustain families and attract new economic opportunities to Pennsylvania.
economy.short: Supports small businesses; advocates family-sustaining wages.

taxes.summary: Voted for and praised the 2026-27 state budget, saying working families deserve a tax system that helps them get ahead, and citing over $200 million in tax relief including an expanded childcare tax credit raising the maximum benefit to $2,100 per family.
taxes.short: Backed 2026-27 budget; cites $200 million tax relief, childcare credit.

education.summary: Says every child deserves access to a high-quality education regardless of ZIP code, and highlighted the 2026-27 budget's $565 million in adequacy formula funding for public schools plus $330 million for Pre-K Counts; his campaign platform calls for adequate funding for all Pennsylvania public schools.
education.short: Supports adequacy funding for public schools and Pre-K investment.

healthcare.summary: Says Pennsylvania's nursing homes face significant financial pressures that put seniors' access to long-term care at risk, noting nearly 70 percent of nursing home residents rely on Medicaid, and highlighted $81 million in additional nursing home funding in the 2026-27 budget.
healthcare.short: Supports Medicaid nursing-home funding to protect seniors' long-term care.

energy.summary: Says Pennsylvania needs strict, enforceable guardrails around data center development so families are not forced to subsidize the cost of powering large tech corporations, and supports bills (HB 1834, HB 2496, HB 2650) establishing ratepayer protections, clean energy investment requirements, and statewide data center standards.
energy.short: Supports data-center guardrails and ratepayer protections on electricity costs.

guns.summary: His campaign public-safety platform supports investing in local law enforcement and expanding mental health and crisis-response resources, with a focus on prevention, accountability, and community trust; it does not detail gun-specific legislation.
guns.short: Supports funding police, mental-health crisis response; no gun-specific platform.
